title: Reader 'horrified' by Truscott photo
article: A letter from Caroline A. Yull, Kingston.

I'm horrified that The Whig chose to run an inflammatory and unnecessary photo from over seven years ago of Samuel Truscott, recently deceased in a senseless incident, on the front top of yesterday's paper. It is unrelated to the more recent news of Mr. Truscott's death and an indignity to the late Mr. Truscott and to his friends and family, who are, no doubt, mourning their loss and preparing for Mr. Truscott's funeral.

Readers had probably figured out the facts surrounding Mr. Truscott's situation by reading the story and didn't need that picture to seal the deal. The photo is gratuitous and plays to the lowest common denominator in us, that atavistic need to see the most base and degrading things that occur.

Pandering to that lowest common denominator has not, in the past, been what The Whig was about, and is definitely not the kind of thing that leads to journalistic awards. I hope that, in future, The Whig will choose more wisely and regain the respect that it once held in this community. This was definitely not the path to that destination.
Perhaps the photo on Page 8 of Amanda Milliken with her award- winning dogs might have been a better choice for a front-page photo, celebrating what's working in the city.
